These IITians are building a made-in-India electric car!  
  
Gurugram-based Blinq Mobility has raised a ₹4.3Cr pre-seed round led by Mumbai and Bengaluru-based early stage venture capital fund 8i Ventures. Blinq Mobility traces its roots back to IIT Delhi where all of the founders were part of the AXLR8R Formula Racing team. They’re building electric cars with battery swapping instead of plug-in charging because they're operating with a fleet-first model. Blinq Mobility will be using their pre-seed to prototype their vehicle platform, build battery swapping infrastructure, and explore pilot deployments with fleet operators and ride-hailing partners.

# All EV Startups in India 2026: The Complete Guide

India's EV boom was built by startups. The complete guide to India's EV startups — vehicle makers, charging, battery and fleet companies — and what each is doing.

Published On 5 Aug 2026, 10:20 pm•By MeraEV Editorial

2 min

Share:

Write a comment

India's EV boom isn't just legacy giants — it's been powered by a wave of startups, from vehicle makers to charging and battery companies. Some are now household names; others are quietly building the ecosystem. Here's the guide to India's EV startups and what each is doing.

## Vehicle-Making Startups

| Startup | Known for |
| --- | --- |
| Ather Energy | Premium scooters, strong software (now listed) |
| Ola Electric | Scale-first scooters (now listed) |
| River | The Indie utility scooter |
| Simple Energy | Long-range Simple One |
| Ultraviolette | Performance bikes (F77) and the Tesseract |
| Matter, Raptee, Avore | Newer bike and scooter makers |

## Charging Startups

* **Statiq, ChargeZone** — building public charging networks.
* **Bolt.Earth** — huge two-wheeler charging footprint.
* **Kazam, ElectricPe** — app-led charging platforms.

## Battery and Swapping Startups

* **Battery Smart** — battery swapping for two- and three-wheelers.
* **Log9, Exponent Energy** — fast-charging cell and pack technology.
* **Others** working on cells, packs and recycling.

## Commercial and Fleet Startups

Names like **Euler Motors and Altigreen** focus on electric cargo and last-mile delivery — a segment where startups have moved fast.

## Why the Startups Matter

* **They drove early innovation** when legacy brands were slow.
* **They built the ecosystem** — charging, swapping, batteries.
* **They keep the market competitive**, pushing everyone forward.

## Expert Verdict

India's EV startups did the early heavy lifting — proving demand, building charging and pushing battery tech. Some, like Ather and Ola, are now public companies; others quietly power the ecosystem. As a buyer, startups can offer fresh tech and sharp pricing, but weigh their scale and support. Either way, they've made India's EV market what it is.

## FAQs

**What are the major EV startups in India?**  
Vehicle makers like Ather, Ola, River, Simple and Ultraviolette, plus charging (Statiq, Bolt.Earth) and battery (Battery Smart, Exponent) startups.

**Are any EV startups now public companies?**  
Yes — Ather Energy and Ola Electric have both listed on the stock market.

**Should I buy from a startup brand?**  
They can offer fresh tech and pricing, but check service reach and support before buying.

India's electric vehicle (EV) startup ecosystem has been gaining significant traction over the past few years. With their focus on cutting-edge technology, scaling production, and building an eco-friendly future, these startups are poised to drive the next wave of India's automotive revolution.
